note: Fix k. Count binary words of length 2k+1 with at least k+1 ones. Bitwise complement pairs every word with a unique word on the opposite strict-majority side, so this set has 2^(2k)=4^k members. If the (k+1)-st one is at position k+j+1, where 0<=j<=k, the preceding k+j bits contain exactly k ones and j zeros (binom(k+j,j) choices), the marked bit is one, and the last k-j bits are arbitrary (2^(k-j) choices). These disjoint cases give the target sum. Works unchanged for k=0.
